**Thursday, November 19, 2026 - **

_**Iran:** International Energy Agency: Iran war causes largest-ever
disruption to global oil and gas trade. Iran says five oil tankers struck
naval mines and caught fire in Hormuz. USS George Washington aircraft carrier
leaves Gulf after three months. President Donald Trump threatens to "wipe out"
Iran over potential dirty bomb attack; U.S. homeland security chief denies
threat. Iran, China, and Russia demand end to military threats before full
resumption of International Atomic Energy Agency inspections. Iranian Foreign
Ministry spokesperson refuses NYT interview over report linking dams to
military infrastructure._

_**Palestine:** Israeli forces kill two Palestinians in Gaza, wound woman.
Israel ends central Gaza ground operation, reopens Salah al-Din Road. Israeli
forces demolish agricultural structures and uproot olive trees in the occupied
West Bank. Eight injured, mosque torched as anti-Palestinian violence
escalates inside Israel. Save the Children: Palestinian victims account for
nearly one third of violations against children worldwide._

_**Yemen:** Ansarallah missile attack damages Saudi investment fund
headquarters. Sixty-four children killed, 64 injured in Yemen as fighting
displaces 330,000 people, UNICEF says._

_**Lebanon:** Israeli airstrikes and artillery shelling continue to hit
southern Lebanon despite ceasefire. U.S. sanctions Lebanese charity,
businessmen, and gold firms over alleged Hezbollah financing._

_**U.S.:** House Democrats elect caucus leaders. House Democrats introduce
bill to give removal orders an expiration date. Maryland Gov. Wes Moore says
Democrats should not tie a government funding bill to ending the Iran war.
U.S. security officials tell Congress they see no evidence cyberattacks caused
tech outages. FBI deputy director declines to name a right-wing domestic
terrorist group when pressed by House Democrats. California Gov. Newsom
unveils plan to regulate AI. Kirkland & Ellis discloses $11.8 million of free
legal work for Trump administration._

_**International:** UN's top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against
the Rohingya. Russian strikes kill at least five across Ukraine. Iraqi court
sentences six French nationals to life in prison for joining ISIL. Somalia
expels UAE ambassador. Ethiopia and Eritrea move troops to border region in
anticipation of war. IAEA chief says North Korea has expanded its Yongbyon
uranium enrichment facility. U.S. and Venezuela sign deal to restore military
ties, War Secretary Pete_ _Hegseth says in Caracas. Reuters: Trump official
suggested Guyana consider ceding territory to Venezuela. Trump, Russian
President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping hold first-ever
trilateral summit in Shenzhen._

**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**

* * *

# Iran

  * **IEA: Iran war causes largest-ever disruption to global oil and gas trade:** The U.S.-Israeli war with Iran [caused](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/middle-east/middle-east-conflict-triggers-biggest-disruption-ever-global-oil-trade-rcna610171) the largest disruption to the global oil and gas trade on record, resulting in cumulative losses of 2.8 billion barrels of oil and 60 billion cubic meters of gas supplies from the Gulf, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said Thursday. The conflict severely restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about 20% of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies.

    * "The energy world will never be the same again as it was before the Iran war," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said. The agency said that the disruption could accelerate a global shift away from fossil fuels, potentially reducing oil demand by 4.4 million barrels per day by 2035 compared with its current-policy projections.

    * Crude shipments through Hormuz fell to approximately 8.5 million barrels per day in November, half their prewar levels, according to data from maritime intelligence firm Kpler, which cautioned that the figure could rise in coming days. Total Middle Eastern oil exports across all routes, including pipelines bypassing the strait, fell to 64% of prewar levels, down from 97% in October.

  * **Iran says five oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in Hormuz:** Five oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday and Thursday after entering "prohibited" shipping routes, according to Iranian authorities. Iran's regular Navy [said](https://en.irna.ir/news/86326369/Three-violating-vessels-catch-fire-after-striking-naval-mines) three tankers caught fire Wednesday in the eastern part of the strait after ignoring warnings and switching off their navigation systems. On Thursday, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy [said](https://en.irna.ir/news/86326732/Two-more-violating-supertankers-catch-fire-in-Strait-of-Hormuz) two additional supertankers struck mines, caught fire and exploded near the strait's southern coast.

  * **USS George Washington aircraft carrier leaves Gulf after three months:** The USS George Washington aircraft carrier reportedly left the Gulf region after a three-month deployment, USNI News reported, citing a U.S. Navy official. Bloomberg reported that the carrier is likely returning to its base in Japan. Its departure follows the arrival of the USS Theodore Roosevelt in the Middle East, where it joined the USS George H.W. Bush. The U.S. military has not officially confirmed the George Washington's departure.

  * **Trump threatens to "wipe out" Iran over potential dirty bomb attack; U.S. homeland security chief denies threat: **President Donald Trump [claimed](https://www.foxnews.com/video/6408573939112) Iran was exploring the development of chemical and biological weapons, saying Tehran was "looking at gases, looking at bio," without providing evidence. Asked about the possibility of an Iranian attack on Washington, Trump told Fox News he did not believe one was likely but warned, "If it does happen, we wipe them out," adding, "I give you my word." Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said during a congressional hearing Wednesday that Iran does not pose an imminent threat of a radioactive "dirty bomb" plot.

  * **Iran, China, and Russia demand end to military threats before full resumption of IAEA inspections:** An end to military attacks and threats, along with credible guarantees against further strikes, is necessary before the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) can fully resume inspections of Iran's nuclear facilities, Iran, China, and Russia said Wednesday. In a joint [statement](https://en.irna.ir/news/86326387/Iran-China-Russia-set-conditions-for-resumption-of-IAEA-verification) delivered at the IAEA Board of Governors meeting in Vienna, the three countries said U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iranian nuclear facilities had made normal verification activities practically impossible.

    * Iran's ambassador to the IAEA, Reza Najafi, warned that Tehran would assess future inspection requests individually based on security considerations and would not grant unrestricted access while military threats persist. "We will not accept being bombed on the one hand while being asked ... to provide detailed information about our materials and sites and grant unrestricted access to them," Najafi said.

    * He also warned that Iran could suspend its safeguards obligations if circumstances required, while maintaining that Tehran had not yet done so. The three countries said Iran had authorized all planned IAEA inspections at the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant in 2026.

  * **Iranian FM spokesperson refuses NYT interview over report linking dams to military infrastructure:** Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei [said](https://x.com/irimfa_spox/status/2123148353567609075?a=GFGt8x_cKTZYWEP17xY&s=46) he rejected an interview request from The New York Times over its reporting on Iranian dams and their alleged links to military infrastructure, accusing the newspaper of promoting narratives that could help justify U.S. and Israeli attacks.

    * The Times [defended](https://x.com/nytimespr/status/2122799480311337360?a=m-IGlY30nqnoh_uIjzE&s=46) its reporting, saying it had accurately cited research and analysis by seven international experts and warning that portraying independent journalism as a pretext for violence was dangerous.

    * However, two experts cited in the article publicly challenged the newspaper's framing. Nima Shokri, an expert on water security at the Hamburg University of Technology, [said](https://x.com/nimashokri_ghi/status/2122440135979749674?a=ujyJcp-c8HieyS8S1Js&s=46) the proximity of dams to military targets neither establishes why they were built nor justifies attacks on them. Kaveh Madani, the former deputy head of Iran's department of environment, published an [article](https://www.forbes.com/sites/kavehmadani/2026/11/17/the-dangerous-logic-of-linking-irans-dams-to-missiles/) in Forbes refuting the Times' conclusions and said in a [post](https://x.com/kavehmadani/status/2122826922807734507?a=8KvzpUzFO3Rcg0iJb58&s=46): "My comments had nothing to do with dams or missiles!"

# Palestine

  * **Israeli forces kill two Palestinians in Gaza, wound woman:** At least one Palestinian was shot dead by Israeli forces on Thursday on Salah al-Din Street in southeastern Gaza City, according to Al Jazeera.**** A Palestinian man also [died](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/19/%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B4%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%AF-%D8%B4%D8%A7%D8%A8-%D9%88%D8%A5%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%A9-%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D9%86%D8%B3%D9%81-%D9%85%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B2%D9%84) Thursday from wounds sustained in an earlier Israeli strike on the Bureij refugee camp, while a woman was shot and wounded in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, WAFA reported.

    * Israeli forces also carried out demolitions overnight in central Gaza, following Wednesday's launch of a new ground operation targeting three areas west of the "yellow line."

  * **Israel ends central Gaza ground operation, reopens Salah al-Din Road:** Israeli forces ended their ground offensive in central Gaza and reopened Salah al-Din Road, Gaza's main north-south artery, to traffic on Thursday, according to COGAT, the Israeli military body overseeing civilian affairs in occupied Palestinian territory. The operation, launched Wednesday near the "yellow line" northeast of Nuseirat refugee camp, forced hundreds of Palestinian families to flee. COGAT said Israeli forces had targeted "terrorist infrastructure" and warned Palestinians against crossing the yellow line or approaching Israeli troops.

    * Hamas condemned the operation and forced evacuations as "a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement," charging Israel of systematically confining Palestinians to an increasingly narrow area of Gaza and urging mediators to intervene immediately.

  * **Israeli forces demolish agricultural structures and uproot olive trees in the occupied West Bank:**

    * **Bethlehem:** Israeli forces [arrested](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/19/%D9%85%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%AB-%D8%AB%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%8D-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D8%AA%D9%82%D9%84-%D8%AE%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%A9-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%86%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%AE%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84) five Palestinians in Beit Fajjar on Thursday, pursued olive pickers in Wadi Saif, and detained workers inside a stone factory, according to WAFA.

    * **Ramallah and Al-Bireh:** Forces [demolished](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/19/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%85-%D9%85%D9%86%D8%B4%D8%A2%D8%AA-%D8%B2%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%88%D9%8A%D9%82%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%B9-%D8%A3%D8%B4%D8%AC%D8%A7%D8%B1) agricultural structures and uprooted olive trees in Deir Ibzi. Late Wednesday, soldiers shot and wounded a 42-year-old Palestinian man in the foot during a raid on central Al-Bireh.

    * **Nablus:** Israeli settlers [attacked](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/19/%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%8A%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%AC%D9%85%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%85%D9%86%D8%B2%D9%84%D8%A7-%D9%82%D9%8A%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A5%D9%86%D8%B4%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D9%88%D9%8A%D8%AD%D8%B7%D9%85%D9%88%D9%86) a house under construction in Qabalan, smashing its windows.

  * **Eight injured, mosque torched as anti-Palestinian violence escalates inside Israel:** Eight Palestinians were [injured](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/18/8-%D8%A5%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%A8%D9%8A%D9%86%D9%87%D9%85-%D9%86%D8%B3%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D8%A5%D8%AB%D8%B1-%D8%AD%D8%A7%D8%AF%D8%AB-%D8%AF%D8%B9%D8%B3-%D9%85%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%AF-%D9%86%D9%81%D8%B0%D9%87) in Kafr Qasim, a Palestinian city inside Israel, on Wednesday when an Israeli driver struck pedestrians at three locations, leaving two seriously wounded and three moderately injured. The town's popular committee described the incident as a deliberate attack fueled by anti-Palestinian incitement, while Israeli police said the driver was under the influence of drugs.

    * Early Thursday, Israeli settlers set fire to a mosque in the village of Al-Dahi, near Nazareth, and spray-painted racist slogans on its walls.

    * Separately, Israeli authorities forced a Palestinian resident of Ar'ara to demolish his unfinished home.

  * **Save the Children: Palestinian victims account for nearly one third of violations against children worldwide:** More than 30% of the total violations against children globally in 2025 were committed against children in the occupied Palestinian territories, [according](https://resourcecentre.savethechildren.net/pdf/SWOC_2026-1711.pdf) to Save the Children's annual global report.

    * Incidents of the denial of humanitarian access to Palestinian children represent more than 70% of the total incidents worldwide, while the killing and maiming of children in the Palestinian territories amounted to almost 40% of the global total. "The scale of harm to children in the occupied Palestinian territory is devastating," the report said.

    * The report also found that Africa is home to the highest number of children living in conflict zones, accounting for about 260 million, or 44% of the global total, with an unprecedented two in five African children impacted.

# Yemen

  * **Ansarallah missile attack damages Saudi investment fund headquarters:** A tower housing the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund in Riyadh [sustained](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261119-skyscraper-in-riyadh-damaged-as-saudi-arabia-reports-surge-in-new-houthi-attacks) damage following a reported Ansarallah missile attack on the capital, AFP reported Thursday. Witnesses said the 80-story tower, the tallest building in Riyadh's financial district, suffered damage to its glass facade and offices across several floors. The damage was reported hours after the Saudi-led coalition announced it had responded to an Ansarallah missile targeting Riyadh and that debris had fallen.

    * Separately, the coalition said its air defenses intercepted and destroyed four Ansarallah ballistic missiles launched toward southern Saudi Arabia.

  * **Sixty-four children killed, 64 injured in Yemen as fighting displaces 330,000 people, UNICEF says:** At least 64 children have been killed and another 64 injured in Yemen since fighting escalated on September 3, UNICEF [said](https://www.unicef.org/press-releases/least-64-children-killed-and-64-injured-yemen-intensified-hostilities-approach-three) Wednesday. More than 330,000 people, including 174,000 children, have been displaced, while at least seven schools and 28 health facilities have been damaged. UNICEF also reported that approximately one in three children screened by its mobile health teams were acutely malnourished.

    * In Taiz City, more than 800,000 people have reportedly been cut off from humanitarian assistance, with water production down nearly 50% and food and fuel prices more than doubling.

# Lebanon

  * **Israeli airstrikes and artillery shelling continue to hit southern Lebanon despite ceasefire:**

    * **Nabatieh:** Israeli warplanes [struck](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/575022/%D8%BA%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%89-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%82%D9%86%D8%B7%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D9%88%D9%85%D9%86%D8%B7%D9%82%D8%A9-%D8%B9%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%AD%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A8%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%B2%D9%88%D8%B7%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B4%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%88%D9%85%D9%8A%D9%81%D8%AF%D9%88%D9%86-2) the Ain Al-Samahiyah area between Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah and Mifdoun on Thursday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Israeli drones also exploded in the Hay Al-Dayaa neighborhood of Nabatieh Al-Fawqa and at a house in Choukine.

    * **Marjeyoun:** Israeli warplanes launched two airstrikes on Qantara, while Israeli forces [fired](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/575061/%D9%82%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%AF%D9%88-%D8%A3%D8%B7%D9%84%D9%82%D8%AA-8-%D9%82%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%A8%D9%84-%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%B4%D8%B1-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%AA%D8%AC%D8%A7%D9%87-%D8%A8%D9%84%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AE%D9%8A%D8%A7%D9%85-2) eight grenades toward Khiam.

  * **U.S. sanctions Lebanese charity, businessmen, and gold firms over alleged Hezbollah financing:** The U.S. Treasury Department [imposed](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0692/) new sanctions Wednesday on the Lebanese Wa Ta'awanu Association, three individuals, and two gold companies over alleged financial ties to Hezbollah. The Treasury described the association as a Hezbollah-affiliated charity that uses humanitarian services to conceal the group's activities. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the sanctions were part of efforts to cut off Hezbollah's financial networks and counter Iranian influence in Lebanon.

# U.S. News

  * **House Democrats elect caucus leaders:** House Democrats [elected](https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/11/18/congress/ted-lieu-democratic-caucus-chair-01172200) California Rep. **Ted Lieu** House Democratic Caucus Chair on Wednesday, making him the highest-ranking Asian American House member ever.

    * Democrats [elected](https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/11/18/congress/clark-aguilar-neguse-win-01172728) Massachusetts Rep. **Katherine Clark** majority leader, making her the first woman to serve as House floor boss when Democrats take control in January. Rep. **Pete Aguilar** of California was elected majority whip, and Rep. **Joe Neguse** of Colorado was elected assistant speaker. All three ran unopposed and won by acclamation.

    * Rep. **Lauren Underwood** [beat](https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/11/18/congress/lauren-underwood-caucus-vice-chair-01172955) Rep. **Sara Jacobs** 143-118 to become House Democratic Caucus vice chair in one of the caucus' rare contested votes. Underwood, 40, co-chairs the caucus's policy and communications arm and has held leadership roles with the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee.

  * **House Democrats introduce bill to give removal orders an expiration date:** Rep. **Lateefah Simon** of California [introduced](https://abcnews.com/Politics/house-dems-introduce-immigration-bill-establishing-10-year/story?id=138185848) the "Protect Our Neighbors Act" Thursday, under which final orders of removal would expire after 10 years for people continuously present in the U.S. with no criminal conviction. Currently, these orders have no expiration date. Under the bill, an immigration judge could renew an expired order only if it had "clear and convincing evidence," and only if the renewal serves the public interest. The bill, co-sponsored by California Reps. **John Garamendi** , **Zoe Lofgren,** and **Juan Vargas** , was inspired by **Harjit Kaur** , a 73-year-old Bay Area grandmother who was detained at an ICE check-in in September 2025 and deported to India under a 2005 removal order. It follows Trump telling "60 Minutes" he would "love to do something on immigration" with Democrats, who take control of Congress in January.

  * **Maryland Gov. Wes Moore says Democrats should not tie a government funding bill to ending the Iran war:** Governor **Wes Moore** , a potential 2028 Democratic presidential candidate, [told](https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/11/18/congress/moore-warns-against-shutdown-01172766) Politico that the Trump administration should end the war but that Democrats' effort to add language ending it to a funding bill is misguided. "I don't know why the American people are being asked to choose between ending a completely rudderless war that we're all paying for and saying, 'Can we please keep the federal government open?'" he said at the National Governors Association's New Governors Leadership Forum in Utah. Democrats in both chambers are pressuring leadership to draw a hard line on Iran war funding in any stopgap bill, which must pass before the Dec. 11 deadline.

  * **U.S. security officials tell Congress they see no evidence cyberattacks caused tech outages:** At a House Homeland Security Committee hearing Wednesday, DHS Secretary **Markwayne Mullin** , Director of National Intelligence **Jay Clayton** , and FBI Deputy Director **Christopher Raia** said the outages that hit airlines, banks, Microsoft services, and the NSA's internal network were not linked. Mullin [said](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/network-outages-cyber-malicious-activity-homeland-security-hearing/) he was "98% confident" they were not malicious activity by foreign adversaries but admitted he had "absolutely not" seen this many outages in so short a time. Clayton called them "separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes," and Raia said there is "no indication whatsoever" of malicious cyber activity.

  * **FBI deputy director declines to name a right-wing domestic terrorist group when pressed by House Democrats:** FBI Deputy Director **Christopher Raia** [told](https://www.washingtonsun.com/legal/fbi-deputy-director-christopher-raia-right-wing-threats) the House Homeland Security Committee on Wednesday that "there isn't" a right-wing organization he would name as a domestic terrorism group, after earlier answering "Yes, sir" when ranking member Rep. **Bennie Thompson** asked if any right-wing groups meet that test. A 2024 National Institute of Justice study, which the Justice Department removed from its website last year, found right-wing extremists have killed more Americans in ideologically motivated attacks than far-left or Islamic extremists.

  * **California Gov. Newsom unveils plan to regulate AI:** California Governor **Gavin Newsom** , a likely 2028 presidential candidate, [released](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/18/newsom-ai-plan-01172739) a report, "AI Safety in 2026 and Beyond," on Wednesday in Washington that would let California officials intervene if AI models risk going rogue, embed independent safety monitors in labs, and order immediate shutdowns if developers don't quickly in "emergency situations." It also calls for giving the state the authority to cap companies' use of automation to develop advanced AI, and requires independent auditors to run regular safety tests on the technology.

  * **Kirkland & Ellis discloses $11.8 million of free legal work for Trump administration: **The white-shoe law firm Kirkland & Ellis [disclosed](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/19/us/politics/kirkland-ellis-law-firm-trump.html) to Congress that it has performed about 6,491 hours of free work valued at $11.8 million for the Commerce Department, the Pentagon, the Postal Service, the International Development Finance Corporation and an investment entity created under the U.S.-Japan trade deal, the New York Times reported on Thursday.

# Other International News

  * **UN 's top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya:** The International Court of Justice [ruled](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/19/un-top-court-finds-myanmar-killed-10000-rohingya-as-it-rules-on-genocide) 9-6 on Thursday that Myanmar "has committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine state, in violation of its obligations under the Genocide Convention." ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa said Myanmar's security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, with evidence showing about 10,000 killed. The court also noted that the soldiers carried out widespread sexual violence and extreme violence against children and attacked people while they fled. The "only reasonable inference," the court argued, is that Myanmar intended to destroy a "substantial part" of the group. The court ordered Myanmar to provide reparations and restitution, including facilitating the safe and voluntary return of Rohingya, finding the missing, and protecting the nation's Rohingya population from persecution. A military crackdown on the mostly Muslim minority in the country has forced more than 730,000 Rohingya to flee to Bangladesh. Thursday's ruling is the first time a state has been found responsible for genocide at the ICJ.

  * **Russian strikes kill at least five across Ukraine:** Russian airstrikes on Wednesday [killed](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/18/russian-attacks-on-ukraine-kill-at-least-five-people) at least four people and wounded 13 others in Odesa, and a separate Russian drone strike in Zaporizhzhia region killed a woman in Kushuhum. Following the Zaporizhzhia strike, local authorities ordered 184 people, including 85 children, evacuated from the nearby village of Balabyne. The strikes came a day after a Ukrainian attack on Russia's Kerch Bridge killed two people and collapsed part of the structure. On Wednesday, Ukraine also hit the Ilsky and Afipsky refineries in Russia's Krasnodar region.

  * **Iraqi court sentences six French nationals to life in prison for joining ISIL:** The Karkh Criminal Court in Baghdad [sentenced](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/18/iraq-sentences-six-french-nationals-to-life-in-prison-for-joining-isil) six French citizens to life on Wednesday for belonging to ISIL (ISIS), with French embassy representatives attending, the Iraqi News Agency reported. Sixteen French nationals have been convicted so far by the court in a trial that began in September, and all but one received life sentences, with the other sentenced to 15 years last month. Iraq received more than 5,700 ISIL detainees from over 60 countries in February after the U.S. moved them from Syria.

  * **Somalia expels UAE ambassador:** Somalia [ordered](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/somalia-orders-uae-ambassador-leave-citing-invasion-2026-11-19/) the ambassador from the United Arab Emirates to leave the country within 72 hours on Thursday, Reuters reported. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud accused the UAE on Tuesday of giving economic and political support to some regional Somali governments opposing the federal government. In January, Somalia said it was terminating all its agreements with the UAE. The UAE trained hundreds of Somali troops from 2014 to 2018 and, according to senior Somali sources, still covers salaries and logistics for about 3,400 Somali military police and special forces in and around the capital, and it has committed hundreds of millions of dollars to ports and military infrastructure along the country's coast.
